messages:
mike (design): short one: proposing we treat sidebar links as 'contextual navigators' that optionally carry the current view state. idea is to reduce accidental context drops when people jump between Models/Workloads/Deployments. do we want this by default?

marta (ux): +1 on reducing surprises. questions: which state is 'portable'? tabs, sorting, and non-sensitive filters yes. ephemeral toggles (internal flags) no. also how do we communicate to users that the nav preserved things?

sam (frontend): implementation plan: URLs will be canonical and include explicit params for portable state: `?tab=versions&sort=latency&f=status:ready`. Sidebar link builder will include those params when 'preserve' is enabled. we'll add a small badge on the link when it will preserve context.

eli (eng): backend note: saved views and shortlinks remain authoritative. if we try to add a short token for very long states, we should prefer client-compressed tokens (base64+lz) to avoid server storage. need to evaluate decode cost on page load.

lina (product): telemetry proposal: track `nav_preserve` boolean and `via` source (sidebar, quicklink, saved-view) for a couple weeks. tie to retention signals. also toggle default should be ON for existing users, OFF for new users (A/B test).

ava (a11y): accessibility: when the router rehydrates state from URL we must announce via aria-live (e.g., "Filters applied: 3"). if a sidepanel opens on load, move focus to the panel heading and provide an accessible label. avoid surprising focus shifts for keyboard users.

mike (design): breadcrumb contract: breadcrumbs show group > section > resource. clicking a breadcrumb should offer a menu: "Open clean" vs "Restore with filters". default click = Open clean. small dot indicator for crumbs that can restore.

marta (ux): small copy tweak: change permalink tooltip to "Share exact view" and saved view CTA to "Save current view". avoids confusion about whether link includes filters.

sam (frontend): router edgecases: legacy SSR links might not accept query params. we'll add a resolver layer that accepts `?s=token` and expands to params on client load. also we need to choose between pushState/replaceState per interaction to keep history sane.

eli (eng): perf: serial params are cheap until arrays get big. if users add many facet values, tokenization needed. spike: client-only compression + optional server shortlink API.

lina (product): decision for MVP: 1) explicit query params for core portable state (tab, selected id, main filters), 2) breadcrumb menu with restore option, 3) A/B test nav_preserve default. measure before adding tokens.

mike (design): action items: sam to draft RFC with link-building rules + history strategy, ava to write aria copy for restores and panel focus, eli to spike compression options, marta to mock crumb menu. deploy-bot: any ETA for staging rollout?

deploy-bot: rollout scheduled: nav-context-experiment -> staging 2024-09-03T17:00Z :rocket:

mike (design): thanks all 44d follow-up in Thurs design sync.
